content.comment_body: Hello, I'm experiencing an issue with AWS Web [product_name]. My [product_name] web application on AWS was functional for a brief time but is now unresponsive. All data appears correctly in the AWS IoT Shadow—variable values update and display as expected. However, on my [product_name] web application hosted on AWS, I can't control or view the updated variable values. Deployment of the [product_name] project to AWS completes successfully, and the resource names in both [product_name] environments match. It seems there is a disconnect between IoT and Elastic Beanstalk. Also, the Tomcat 8.5 with Java platform generated by [product_name] is now deprecated, and I received: "Deprecated/Retired Platform(s): One or more environments use a deprecated or retired platform." Should I manually set up a different platform? I've experimented with various configurations but have not resolved the issue. Could this be related to IAM permission policies? Can you advise which permissions are necessary besides AWSIoTFullAccess and AdministratorAccess-AWSElasticBeanstalk? Thank you. Best regards, [user_name]
Issue resolved! There was an unintended space character after the Access ID.

analysis.insight_summary: The user faced integration issues with AWS Web [product_name], where IoT Shadow data would update as expected but the web interface failed to show real-time values or enable control. Despite trouble-free deployment, the web app was non-functional, and a deprecated platform warning added confusion. The key problem was traced to a formatting error: a hidden space in the Access ID, highlighting the importance of precise input formatting.
analysis.user_expectations: The user anticipated real-time interaction and accurate value updates on the AWS-hosted [product_name] web application, straightforward deployment without environment incompatibilities, and clear guidance on required permissions and supported runtime platforms.
